content: Etrasimod has not been studied in combination with antineoplastic, immune-modulating, or non-corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapies. Co-administration of etrasimod with such therapies should be avoided during and in the weeks following its administration due to the potential risk of additive immunosuppressive effects and increased susceptibility to infections. When etrasimod is used in combination with certain drugs, such as avelumab, axalimogene filolisbac, axicabtagene ciloleucel, azacitidine, azathioprine, balstilimab, baricitinib, basiliximab, belatacept, belinostat, belzutifan, bendamustine, bevacizumab, bexarotene, binimetinib, bleomycin, blinatumomab, bortezomib, bosutinib, brentuximab vedotin, brexucabtagene autoleucel, busulfan, cabazitaxel, cabozantinib, camrelizumab, cannabidiol, capecitabine, or other similar agents, there is a risk of increased immunosuppressive effects. This can lead to a heightened risk of infections. In such cases, alternative therapies should be considered, or the combination should be avoided. Etrasimod may cause transient decreases in heart rate and delays in atrioventricular (AV) conduction when initiated. While concomitant use of etrasimod with stable beta-blocker therapy has not shown additive effects on heart rate reduction, the risk of additive heart rate reduction when initiating beta-blocker therapy with stable etrasimod treatment or when used with other heart rate-lowering drugs remains unknown. Close monitoring is advised in such scenarios. Etrasimod may also increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes when co-administered with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or other QT-prolonging agents. This necessitates careful monitoring and potential modification of therapy. In patients who are CYP2C9 poor metabolizers, co-administration of etrasimod with moderate to strong CYP2C8 inhibitors may lead to increased exposure to etrasimod. This interaction should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be considered.
